evidence: [I] model (event-driven simulation; an exact model of the contract semantics: F0.10 derived back-off, and F0.15 stored back-off in the +SW variants); success curve interpolated from v0.3 §13.8
assumptions: The attacker guesses at every allowed moment; all guesses are wrong (the success probability comes separately from the curve). It uses only the K-track: the recovery track requires a bond and shares the common budget (K56), so it gives no advantage.
First wrong guess at t = 0; the owner reacts r after the first notification.

rotate: the owner verifies the rotation with K+P (without D on the K-track, waiting out the attacker's back-off; with D on the lane, without waiting); the rotation executes after 24 h. K45 (only with D/recovery helper) closes the K-track as soon as it is verified.

escape: the owner starts an escape with K (no PIN). K44: anonymous guessing closes immediately. Without K44 the attacker keeps guessing for 30 days (if the PIN is found, the escape is cancelled with K+P).
unrestrict: r after each restriction the owner lifts it with the PIN (in v03 the counter is reset every time; in K43 the score is kept and the owner's PIN updates the last-attempt time).
Decay (K43): fixed calendar, −1 every 7 days; the phase φ of the first boundary is scanned on an hourly grid and the worst phase is reported (guessesMinMedianMax: over the phases).
Below 10 guesses the success probability is linear from 0 (the real curve is concave; higher for the first guesses).

+SW (F0.15, stored wait): the back-off end is saved when a guess is submitted and recomputed from the last attempt with the refunded score on a correct result; a decay boundary never shortens a running back-off. Rows without +SW model the F0.10 derived back-off.

f016.evidence: [I] model (the same event-driven simulation; bond = PolicyMath.ownerBondFor at the score counted on submission)
assumptions: Only K is stolen; the thief guesses at every allowed moment and pays each bond from its own funds (a direct call by K; the account's balance can never pay it). Every bond of a wrong guess stays in the account.
Worst case for the owner: the decay phase with the most guesses, and among those the cheapest bonds.
Human PIN: the Markert curve without a blocklist (P(10) = 6.5%, P(30) = 8.9%, P(100) = 13.3%; linear below 10). The app's short reject list only lowers it, so the curve overstates the thief's odds.
Random PIN: uniform over the PINs randomPin() can return (not on the list, no warning); the thief knows the generator and never repeats a guess: P(n) = n / space.

Expected gain = P(PIN found in the window) × account value: an upper bound. Finding the PIN is not yet moving the funds: a PIN transfer waits its delay (1 h; 48 h above L_big) and the owner can still escape. In the 'escape within 1 h' scenario the escape also cancels every pending op, so the realistic gain there is about zero.
Expected bond loss = Σ (1 − P(i)) · bond_i: guess i is made only if the earlier ones failed, and its bond is refunded if it is right.
rationalThief: the number of guesses k that maximizes P(k)·V − loss(k) (0 = guessing does not pay).
